card.name: Pre-procedure instructions: what you may need to do
card.fires_on: Words like "to", "needed", "asked" or "need" that lead into an instruction about what a patient must do or have done before a test or procedure. Seen in preparation lists about stopping medications, fasting, or required tests.

modes.label: Stop medicines before procedure
modes.description: The word "to" after "necessary for you" or "asked", introducing an instruction to stop something.
modes.example: It may be necessary for you<< to>> stop these medications prior to the procedure.

modes.label: Test or sample requirement
modes.description: A verb of requirement in a lab-test or pregnancy-test preparation sentence.
modes.example: How the test is performed: A blood sample is<< needed>>. For information on how this is done

modes.label: Do I need to ask
modes.description: Question-style prep items where a verb follows "need to" or "or".
modes.example: Do I need to<< have>> an enema or take a laxative

card.writes: It promotes words about issuing or certifying documents (e.g. 证明, 出具, copies), which is not a clear fit with the text; the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up on the small words that introduce what a patient is required or asked to do before a procedure or test.
